# Pulse task #2873: Regenerate the end-user changelog for every new local merge

Operation: e68256e798ec8bf8c34256b77dd521df
Assignee: PORTALSURFER (Pulse #1, GitHub ID 41680373)

User request 19 October 2026: fix local CI so the AI-generated end-user changelog is regenerated for every new merge. Existing completed2804/PR410 implements generation+viewer, not this automatic current-merge coverage. Root inspected clean local53ad: local-ci.py changelog step only validates --if-present; --prepare-changelog is separate opt-in that exits before checks; validate_current without --through accepts old coverage. Existing generated.json has one batch through cb8befc4f2dd19d0af1fd02932cb52941653b479, so newer main merges do not automatically regenerate notes. This is a focused workflow/freshness correction; preserve original2804/PR410 and all retained notes, dataset format/provenance/viewer/licensing/source history.

Outcome: the repository-owned local CI/merge workflow automatically prepares/updates concise AI-written user-facing features/fixes/improvements for every newly integrated merge, and checks require appropriate fresh coverage before a candidate can be presented as qualified/delivered with current notes. Reuse configured authorized Codex/account generation route, no new service/billing/API fallback/hosted CI. Never substitute a static template and call it AI. Internal-only changes may legitimately produce no visible entries while still recording covered range; deduplicate, retain all history and handle repeated invocation/rebuild/idempotence.

Exact-source requirement: generation and generated-data commit/freeze happen BEFORE final required CI and merge; no tracked notes rewritten after checks while claiming old source is qualified. Define candidate/actual merge source mapping explicitly, including changelog-only commits and merge commits so generation does not recurse forever or create a catch-up commit for every metadata commit. Do not force all ordinary independent offline test invocations to call a model or overwrite dirty source; introduce/coherently update the normal local merge-preparation entry point and freshness gate, with an explicit actionable generation result on missing/stale notes. The actual normal merger must use it, not merely expose another optional flag. No global Pulse deployment engine, GitHub Actions or unrequested Git hooks/background service.

Handle current backlog since cb8 coverage with bounded chronological ranges/per-merge batches if necessary, preserving provenance/no silent truncation/gaps/overlaps. AI timeout/unavailable/cloud proxy/malformed output must retain last good notes and report incomplete generation; configured Mac execution import remains supported but exported packets alone are not success. No generator on app startup. Existing packaging must embed the fresh validated dataset and viewer gets those notes after the corresponding build. First baseline, empty user changes, merge/rebase history change, concurrent publisher/stale dataset, dirty/unpublished work, interrupted/retried generation and renamed/new branch cases have finite explicit behavior.

Acceptance: real temporary-Git integration tests exercise TWO successive actual merges through the normal local preparation/validation path; each new user-facing change updates coverage exactly once, rerun no duplicate, internal/changelog-only input cannot loop; stale/missing/error/offline preserve last good data and cannot be reported fresh. Injected model fixture is only orchestration test; an actual configured inference run/source-bound generated output is required separately before claiming live automatic AI regeneration. Relevant existing generator/provenance/packaging/local-CI tests and full final exact-candidate checks must pass. Preserve current21 validation/locks/target budgets and --test opt-in launcher behavior.

Existing general cloud executor takes this after the newly prioritized launcher2806/PR412 coherent handoff; current469 test-oracle checkpoint first and already accepted474 source preserved. Inspect and propose precise preparation/freeze/coverage contract before changing shared local-CI/merge contract; one writer, no fourth worker. Solemerger owns integration/final checks/merge and must adopt final normal workflow; source acceptance is separate from actual notes/build/native acceptance. Root local currentapp untouched. No app/process/build/install/signing/data/credential changes are authorized by this workflow request.

ticket.title: Plan Hex release channels with rolling and frozen changelogs
ticket.description:
CURRENT USER DIRECTION — 19 October 2026 (supersedes the original every-merge regeneration/gate implementation brief below).
PLANNING ONLY: design a repository-owned local release pipeline with lightweight merges, a rolling Unreleased changelog and immutable release snapshots. Do not implement the former synchronous generator/freshness gate during every merge. Neither scheduled nightly automation nor external publication/deployment is started by this planning request.

Recommended channels:
1. Development/local: each actual merge records its immutable source/PR identity and contributes user-facing entries to rolling Unreleased. Generation/append is a recoverable separate preparation activity; model unavailability must not block otherwise-qualified ordinary merges. No model call on application startup. Local dev builds consume current draft notes with explicit coverage status and source/build identity; dev is the moving development state, not a separately stabilized release.
2. Nightly: optional dated snapshots of verified main, e.g. 0.1.0-nightly.20261019.1, only when source changed and required local checks/build/signing pass. Each published snapshot/notes/artifact is immutable. The rolling Unreleased ledger continues. A real nightly schedule later requires explicit user scheduling/setup; do not enable hosted/paid CI.
3. Beta: explicit stabilization cut for a target version, e.g. 0.1.0-beta.1, beta.2, beta.3. Freeze scope at beta cut; fixes produce NEW immutable numbered beta snapshots rather than altering beta1. Main may continue next-version development, with provenance-backed fix propagation when branches diverge. Each beta shows cumulative notes since prior stable and optionally a small delta since previous beta; cutting beta does not erase the stable version's unreleased history.
4. Stable: explicit promotion/cut from accepted release source after required optimized build/verification/signing. Freeze versioned dated notes and exact artifact/source identity for 0.1.0; archive Unreleased into that stable version and continue the next target bucket. Never rewrite a published version/artifact. New fixes require a new version. Metadata changes/rebuilds must be tracked honestly; tested candidate is not silently relabeled as a different binary/version.

Changelog contract: append/deduplicate per actual merged change, then consolidate concise AI-written features/fixes/improvements for readers. Internal-only merges still record coverage but can have no visible note. Preserve all prior notes and canonical PR/source links internally; product notes omit implementation jargon and unmerged/shipped claims. Durable generation backlog/cursor, bounded per-merge catchup and atomic retry prevent missing/duplicated notes. Source/build/coverage identities remain distinguishable. Release cut requires complete relevant coverage; ordinary merges don't wait for generation. Draft regeneration never rewrites frozen historical snapshots. Changelog-only bookkeeping cannot trigger infinite self-generation. No legacy migrations/backward compatibility commitment during current Hex/Yield alpha.

Pipeline plan should define collection vs generation vs release-cut vs local validation/build vs optional publication/installation, selecting exact source first and freezing all build inputs before final verification. Keep existing compiler/source checks and current ordinary merge authority; do not add Pulse permits/activation engines or treat ticket Done as deployment evidence. Retain configured authorized Codex inference route, no new service/API-billed fallback/purchase. Failed model/build/signing/publication leaves last good release available and reports actual state. Updater selects an explicit channel and channel-specific monotonic ordering; do NOT lexically rank nightly/beta across channels or silently move stable users onto pre-releases.

Planning acceptance: document finite commands/states, version examples, Unreleased/snapshot data model, branch/catchup/dedup/empty/retry/concurrent cases, same-path optimized native packaging and exact artifact identity, channel selection, alpha policy, current real generation capability, local scheduling constraints, and a staged implementation ticket breakdown after design review. Source-specific tests later must cover repeated merges, beta1→beta2→stable and next-development changes without losing/duplicating entries or mutating snapshots. Include real configured AI generation proof when implemented, not just fixtures. No additional worker or source changes now.

User's wording initially alternated beta/nightly; recommendation keeps BOTH because nightly tracks development while beta stabilizes a named target. Standard references: https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/ (Unreleased then versioned sections), https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html (prerelease identifiers, zero-version development, published version immutability). These guide release naming/history and do not impose 1.0 compatibility during alpha.
